To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
treatment with pHLA constructs is highly effective in female mice with MCI, and that these pHLA constructs also improve post-MCAO USV in females.

the humanized recombinant TCR ligand RTL1000 is effective in female mice after transient cerebral ischemia, with the same or better outcomes as in male animals, and also protects the ability of mice to vocalize normally, a behavior that is relevant to human stroke recovery.
humanized recombinant T cell receptor ligands protect the female brain after experimental stroke.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel, humanized recombinant T cell receptor ligands for the treatment of stroke.
developing a novel class of T cell receptor-like immunomodulatory agents for stroke therapy.
the development and evaluation of new therapeutic agents to treat acute brain injury in both males and females.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

RTL1000 and HLA-DR1-MOG-55-55 constructs were both effective in reducing ischemic infarct volume in female mice, and that RTL1000 was effective in improving post-ischemic vocalization capability in female mice.
the novel non-polimorphic pMHC construct (DRa1-MOg-35-55) is effective for treating female stroke, and is as effective as RTL1000, which is a more expensive and difficult to produce construct.
the pMHC constructs are effective for treating ischemic stroke in both sexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pMHC ligands, when given at the appropriate dose, can be effective in both male and female stroke patients.
the RTL1000 construct is effective for treatment of both male and female mice with transient cerebral ischemia, but that the non-polymorphic HLA-DR1-MOG construct was less effective for females.
the pMHC constructs are effective in females, but that the optimal dose is higher in female mice than in males, as was previously reported.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pMHC-based therapeutics are highly effective in both males and females with experimental stroke.
pMHC-based immunotherapies may have a role in the management of stroke in both sexes, and that the female brain may be particularly sensitive to these agents.
the sex of the patient is a critical factor in determining the most effective treatment strategy.
